text:
maria.p: Quick sync — thinking out loud about smoothing enforcement across endpoints. Right now chat has a tight per-key burst bucket, embeddings use a larger shared bucket, streaming is throttle-y and rerank is kinda in-between. We keep hitting noisy 429s for short spikes (user types a 4k prompt) and it skews our telemetry. Thoughts?

lee_sre: +1 we see a bunch of 429 spikes that are single-request huge token counts. Hard to tell in dashboards whether it's a bad client or real load.

david.k: Can we differentiate by endpoint token footprint? Chat requests are often many tokens in/out; embeddings are small per request but high rps. Rerank is quick bursts with lots of short requests. Streaming needs per-connection pacing.

sasha_p: From product POV we want predictable UX: small bursts shouldn't break sessions. But we also need to protect capacity. Maybe smoothing window or token-budget smoothing per minute?

maria.p: Proposed pattern: introduce a thin smoothing layer that converts per-endpoint semantics into a unified enforcement model. High-level: per-key overall budget -> per-endpoint soft limits with spillover rules -> enforcement action (delay, 429, or degrade).

tim.ops: Do we have a diagram for spillover? e.g., if embeddings overrun, can it borrow from org-level unused chat budget? That seems risky.

maria.p: Not borrow blindly. Idea is prioritized spillover with hysteresis. Example policy order: 1) chat (priority high for active sessions) 2) streaming (keep connections alive with pacing) 3) rerank (best-effort) 4) embeddings (batch-friendly, can queue). Spillover only when org-level headroom > threshold and only for short windows.

lee_sre: Implementation note: prefer token-token (not requests) accounting for fairness. We already have per-token counters in the meter; need a small smoothing buffer + leaky-bucket that can absorb single-request peaks then backfill accounting.

quota-bot: FYI: recent commit to meter-service added per-endpoint labels: endpoint=chat|embeddings|rerank|streaming.

maria.p: Good — that helps telemetry. Another UX question: what enforcement responses should API return? currently 429 JSON is generic. Should we extend to `429: reason: "burst_smoothing:delayed"` or include suggested retry-after semantics?

david.k: Include a machine-readable code + human message. Eg {code: "ep_burst_delayed", retry_after_ms: 500} for brief delays; {code: "ep_quota_exceeded", retry_after_ms: null} for hard rejects. This helps clients back off smarter.

sasha_p: Also surface on Console: per-endpoint burst heatmap + 95th percentile smoothing latency so teams can see if their chat sessions got delayed vs dropped.

tim.ops: For rollout: feature flag per org + canary to 5% orgs. Telemetry we need: count of smoothing events, average delay, spilled tokens, and 429 v delayed split. Also tag by model and sequence length bucket.

lee_sre: Edge case: streaming keep-alives. If we delay tokens mid-stream, it can break client timeouts. For streaming we should prefer pacing (throttle token cadence) instead of a 429/delay. Implementation could return a header hinting to SDKs: `X-Stream-Pace: 75pct` and SDKs smooth generation.

maria.p: Sketch of config (informal):

```
policy:
  per_key_budget: tokens_per_minute: 20000
  endpoints:
    chat: {priority: 100, burst_buffer: 2000, smoothing_window_ms: 2000, action: delay}
    streaming: {priority: 90, burst_buffer: 1000, smoothing_window_ms: 100, action: pace}
    rerank: {priority: 50, burst_buffer: 1500, smoothing_window_ms: 500, action: reject_or_delay}
    embeddings: {priority: 20, burst_buffer: 5000, smoothing_window_ms: 10000, action: queue}
  spillover_threshold_pct: 20
```

lee_sre: That looks workable. burst_buffer units as tokens, smoothing windows tuned per endpoint.

david.k: A couple of implementation choices: where to place the smoothing layer? API gateway vs meter-service vs serving runtime. Gateway is fast but stateless; meter-service centralizes accounting. My vote: gateway for latency-critical quick decisions (single-request burst acceptance) and meter-service for longer-term queueing/spillover coordination.

maria.p: Agree. Gateway decides immediate accept/delay for small bursts using tokenized leaky-bucket, posts events to meter-service which performs conceding/longer queue actions.

sasha_p: For Console telemetry, can we show the last 24h smoothing events and a per-route breakdown? Also a per-org setting page to tune priorities for their use-case?

maria.p: Yes — default priorities reasonable; allow enterprise override in Private & Dedicated only. Public hosted keeps fixed priorities to avoid abuse.

tim.ops: Action items: 1) david + lee iterate on gateway leaky-bucket prototype (PR targeting next week). 2) maria + sasha mock Console UX for heatmap and per-endpoint rules. 3) add extended 429 codes to API contract (post RFC). 4) canary plan + telemetry dashboard (tim).

david.k: I'll open a draft PR and add integration tests for token accounting with sequence-length variability.

lee_sre: I'll add a Prometheus / OTEL set for smoothing events and a Grafana panel prototype.

maria.p: Great. Let's aim for a small internal canary by EOW next sprint. If anyone has objections to the priority ordering or the action mapping, speak now.

sasha_p: No objections from product. Please document expected client SDK fallback behaviors so we can set SDK defaults.

maria.p: Thanks all.

quota-bot: Note: created issue #PLAT-789 (smoothing-layer prototype) assigned to david.k,lee_sre, due 2026-04-02.
